clue.text: Boldly confront air conditioning price

blocks.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for air conditioning
a price is what something costs

explanation.surface: Someone storms up to a shop counter to complain about what the air conditioning unit costs.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly, often aggressively.

clue.text: Surprise when wife leaves town? Sort of

indicators.note: when someone leaves a place they are no longer there, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
W is the usual abbreviation for wife
taken as written before the cut
the suffix -ish means 'sort of', as in reddish

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing about what a town becomes when a wife moves away.
explanation.walkthrough: Take W out of TOWN to leave TON, then sandwich it: AS + TON + ISH = ASTONISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze or surprise greatly; both are verbs.

clue.text: Actor vainly working to be perceptive

indicators.note: something working is in motion, so these letters are set going into a fresh order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A vain actor tries hard to come across as insightful.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant person supposedly sees beyond normal senses, so loosely the word means highly perceptive.

clue.text: Just one swimmer

blocks.note: first meaning: only, single, as in the only survivor
second meaning: a flatfish

explanation.surface: Only a single swimmer turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means only or single, and a sole is also a flat sea fish, a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Cold, attending a search in underground area

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to be attending an event is to be at it
taken as written
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A shivering searcher hunts through some subterranean space.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of tunnels and chambers, an area below ground.

clue.text: One missing a competition directed inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for directed sits within the word for competition

blocks.note: taken as written
a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee
sent means directed somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone sent into a contest fails to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Competition' is a spelling-bee-style contest; 'directed' is the past tense, as in sent on an errand.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is not present, someone missing from where they should be.

clue.text: Change euro at Nice — lots, one's specialty

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A traveller swaps euros on the Riviera, as if a currency expert.
explanation.walkthrough: In the definition, lots are items for sale at a sale room, not 'a great deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer sells goods in numbered lots, so lots are that person's speciality.

clue.text: Flier, funny guy, doffing cap

indicators.note: doffing a cap removes what sits on top, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: someone hilarious is 'a howl'

explanation.surface: A comic pilot takes off his hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl is a bird, and birds are fliers.

clue.text: Blast introduction of big energy charge

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of big
E is the physics symbol for energy
a rate is a charge, as in a fixed price

explanation.surface: A complaint about a large new energy tariff being brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast someone is to criticise them fiercely, which is to berate them.

clue.text: Previous head of religious house

blocks.note: first meaning: earlier
second meaning: a monk in charge of a priory

explanation.surface: The former leader of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier, and a prior is the superior of a priory or a deputy to an abbot.

clue.text: Roof worker maybe taking in artist's promotional material

indicators.note: taking in means admitting something inside, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a tiler may work on roofs; 'maybe' marks it as one example
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A roofer helps carry a painter's advertising leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a short preview advertising a film, a kind of promotional material.

clue.text: Rule as caretaker originally — unusual to be there for long time

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so the word keeps just its first letter
something unusual is out of the normal run, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
first letter of caretaker

explanation.surface: A temporary ruler oddly hangs on in office for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses a rarer sense of the word: lasting for an age or century, as in a secular trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular, from Latin saeculum (an age), can describe something persisting over a very long period.

clue.text: Informer upset complainer

blocks.note: first meaning: a police spy or grass
a further meaning: to annoy, as a verb
second meaning: a grumbler

explanation.surface: A snitch has upset someone who moans.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition: British slang uses the word for an informer, a grumbler, and, as a verb, to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nark is a police informer and also a persistent complainer.

clue.text: Exactly corresponding to company scene maybe

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
a scene, a public fuss, is one kind of incident

explanation.surface: Something matching a company's setting precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincident means occurring together or agreeing exactly, so in precise correspondence.

clue.text: Sparks article, nice, lively

indicators.note: lively suggests bustling movement, so these letters are jumbled around

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A review praises a piece of writing as sparkling, pleasant and lively.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparks is British slang for an electrician; it looks like a verb or plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is the traditional nickname for an electrician or radio operator.

clue.text: Romance, lie, unfortunately — there's formal pattern to it

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going awry, so these letters fall out of place

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A love affair built on deceit follows a sadly predictable script.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ceremonial follows a fixed ritual or formal procedure, a set pattern.

clue.text: Push large tool

blocks.note: a shove is a push
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An order to push a big implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a digging implement, a common garden tool.

clue.text: Move aimlessly, somewhat lame and erratic

indicators.note: somewhat means only to some extent, so just part of the following words is used

blocks.note: running across the words lame, and and erratic

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about, limping and unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander without a fixed course, like a winding river.

clue.text: Open new version of fans' tune

indicators.note: a new version reworks the original, so these letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Supporters launch a remixed anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a catch or button is to undo it, letting it open; both are verbs.

clue.text: In thrifty manner following game by missing out friend

indicators.note: missing out means leaving something away, so those letters are removed from the game word

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
rugby is a ball game
taken as written; these are the letters dropped
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A careful spender leaves a friend out of a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: RUGBY without BY leaves RUG, so F + RUG + ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugally means sparingly with money or resources, which is how a thrifty person acts.

clue.text: Sheet worker's colourful public display

blocks.note: a sheet of paper is a page
a worker ant; the 's stands for 'is' linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A paper worker puts on a vivid show.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is an elaborate public spectacle, often with costumes and processions.

clue.text: Close by accepting court's drink

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one word holds the other within it

blocks.note: near means close by
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A tipple taken near the royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods, and also a name for any delicious drink or fruit juice.

clue.text: Conservative with papers is being frank

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
and means together with
ID: identity papers

explanation.surface: A Tory holding documents speaks openly.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means open and honest in speech, synonymous with frank.

clue.text: Excellent group

blocks.note: first meaning: top-quality
second meaning: a set of pupils or a category

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a band; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, class means first-rate, and a class is a group of students or a category.

clue.text: Something done at island ramble not half dangerous legally

indicators.note: not half means half the word is dropped, keeping only its second part

blocks.note: an act is something done
Iona is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides
taken as written before halving

explanation.surface: A walk on an island is risky only in a legal sense.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMBLE loses its first half, RAM, leaving BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something actionable gives grounds for a lawsuit, so it is legally risky.

clue.text: Indication one's engaged in racecourse betting area

blocks.note: first meaning: an engagement band worn on the finger
second meaning: the bookmakers' enclosure at a racecourse

explanation.surface: A newly engaged punter flashes a token among the bookies.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement ring signals betrothal, and the betting enclosure at a racecourse is called the ring.

clue.text: Large room in hotel? Quite

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
all can mean quite or completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A query whether a hotel has a big room, answered 'quite'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall is a large room for gatherings, such as a banqueting hall.

clue.text: Writer repelled attack at first

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a raid is an attack
first is written 1st, with I standing for the 1

explanation.surface: An author fought off an assault at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like a first-letter signal, but only 'first' gives letters: 1ST read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist writes a diary, so is a kind of writer.

clue.text: Regularly visited Afghan military commander

indicators.note: regularly visited means calling at every other stop, so alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of Afghan

explanation.surface: A general often called on by an Afghan.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a title for a commander or chief officer in Ottoman Turkey and neighbouring regions.

clue.text: Second discussion group one included for King Charles, say

indicators.note: included means put inside, so the letter for one goes within the group word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a panel is a group discussing a topic
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A second debating panel admits a member to discuss the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a monarch, but a King Charles is a breed of toy spaniel.
explanation.definitionFit: The King Charles spaniel is a dog breed, an example of the wider category.

clue.text: After return, finish, adopting unexpectedly ideal time limit

indicators.note: after a return something faces back the way it came, so this word runs backwards
unexpectedly suggests a surprising turn, so these letters are rearranged
adopting means taking in, so one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to finish is to end
taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: On coming back, wrap up by taking on an unexpectedly perfect cut-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ideal' looks like praise for the time limit, but it is just the letters to be mixed and tucked inside the turned-round word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the latest time by which something must be done, a time limit.

clue.text: Lots losing heart — penalty out of order

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle is taken away, so the central letter goes
out of order means not in the right sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; its middle letter is the fourth of seven

explanation.surface: Plenty of disheartened players face a penalty for misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: PENALTY drops its central A, and PENLTY is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty means a great amount, which is what lots means.
